owner.description: Address that can add new gauges or stop them

Decimal.description:
A fixed-point decimal value with 18 fractional digits, i.e. Decimal(1_000_000_000_000_000_000) == 1.0

guardian.description: Stop-only safety authority. Only the owner may resume.

execution_window_seconds.description: Bounded interval after voting closes during which execution may occur.

retained_option.description: Optional non-project sink. It counts as an affirmative ballot signal but is excluded from project selection and adapter execution.

adapter.description: Address of contract to serve gauge-specific info (AdapterQueryMsg)

epoch_size.description: Frequency (in seconds) the gauge executes messages, typically something like 7*86400

max_options_selected.description: Maximum number of Options to make the selected set. Needed even with `min_percent_selected` to provide some guarantees on gas usage of this query.

min_percent_selected.description: Minimum percentage of votes needed by a given option to be in the selected set. If unset, there is no minimum percentage, just the `max_options_selected` limit.

reset_epoch.description: If set, the gauge can be reset periodically, every `reset_epoch` seconds.

snapshot_policy.description: Required in epoch-snapshot mode and rejected in hook mode.

oneOf.description: Updates gauge voting power in Token DAOs when a user stakes or unstakes
Updates gauge voting power in NFT DAOs when a user stakes or unstakes
Updates gauge voting power for membership changes
This creates a new Gauge, returns CreateGaugeReply JSON-encoded in the data field. Can only be called by owner
Allows owner to update certain parameters of GaugeConfig. If you want to change next_epoch value, you need to use migration.
Freezes voting, reset, and epoch execution for a gauge. Voting-power hooks continue updating existing votes so accounting remains current.
Owner-only: resumes voting, reset, and epoch execution for a stopped gauge.
Publicly opens the next epoch at one historical power height.
Publicly terminalizes an unexecuted epoch at or after its deadline.
Owner-only terminal recovery for an unrecoverable adapter or migration failure. The reason is persisted in the terminal outcome.
Owner-only future-epoch policy update.
Public bounded cleanup of one terminal epoch.

Resets all votes on a given gauge if it is configured to be periodically reset and the epoch has passed. One call to this will only clear `batch_size` votes to prevent gas exhaustion. Call repeatedly to clear all votes.
Try to add an option. Error if no such gauge, or option already registered. Otherwise check adapter and error if invalid. Can be called by anyone, not just owner
Allows the owner to remove an option. This is useful if the option is no longer valid or if the owner wants to remove all votes from a valid option.
Place your vote on the gauge. Can be updated anytime

votes.description: The options to put my vote on, along with positive weights whose sum is at most 1.0. Any unused weight is intentionally unallocated. "None" means remove existing votes and abstain

oneOf.description: Takes a sample of the current tally and execute the proper messages to make it work

Owner-only: register a contract address to receive [`GaugeVoteHookMsg`](crate::hooks::GaugeVoteHookMsg) submessages on every `PlaceVotes`. Subscribers receive `reply_on_error`-style submessages — a hook that errors is auto-unregistered.
Owner-only: drop a previously-registered hook subscriber.

Addr.description:
A human readable address.

In Cosmos, this is typically bech32 encoded. But for multi-chain smart contracts no assumptions should be made other than being UTF-8 encoded and of reasonable length.

This type represents a validated address. It can be created in the following ways 1. Use `Addr::unchecked(input)` 2. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_validate(input)?` 3. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_humanize(canonical_addr)?` 4. Deserialize from JSON. This must only be done from JSON that was validated before such as a contract's state. `Addr` must not be used in messages sent by the user because this would result in unvalidated instances.

This type is immutable. If you really need to mutate it (Really? Are you sure?), create a mutable copy using `let mut mutable = Addr::to_string()` and operate on that `String` instance.
